--- title: "Window Functions" subtitle: "≈ grouped `mutate()` · dplyr window functions · slider" jupyter: python3 --- A window function returns one value per input row, computed from a set of related rows: the row's group, the rows before it, or the rows within three hours of it. [Expressions & Contexts](../core/expressions.qmd#sec-expr-contexts) introduced `.over()` as grouped `mutate()`. This chapter covers the rest: how a window is partitioned, ordered and mapped back; offsets, cumulative functions, ranks and rolling windows; and the places where row order silently changes the answer. ## In tidyverse {#sec-win-tidyverse} ```r library(dplyr) library(nycflights13) flights |> mutate( day_avg = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE), # aggregate, broadcast back day_rank = min_rank(desc(dep_delay)), # rank within the day .by = c(month, day) ) flights |> arrange(time_hour, minute) |> # order the frame first ... mutate(prev_delay = lag(dep_delay), .by = tailnum) # ... then lag within each plane weather |> mutate(temp_3h = slider::slide_index_dbl(temp, time_hour, mean, .before = hours(2)), .by = origin) ``` dplyr spreads a window over three places: `.by` partitions, `arrange()` (or `order_by =`) orders, and the function picks the frame. Most window functions see the whole group, cumulative ones see the group up to the current row, and a sliding frame needs slider. Polars puts all three into one expression: | Part of the window | SQL | dplyr | Polars | |---|---|---|---| | Partition | `PARTITION BY g` | `.by = g` | `.over("g")` | | Order | `ORDER BY t` | `arrange(t)` first; `lag(x, order_by = t)`; `order_by(t, cumsum(x))` | `.over(..., order_by="t")` | | Frame: last *k* rows | `ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` | `slider::slide_dbl(.before = 2)` | `.rolling_mean(3)` | | Frame: last 3 hours | `RANGE` frame | `slider::slide_index_dbl()` | `.rolling_mean_by("t", "3h")` | | Rows returned | one per input row | one per input row | `mapping_strategy=` decides | : The parts of a window {.striped} ## Mental model {#sec-win-model} ```text pl.col("x").cum_sum().over("g", order_by="t") input ① partition by g ② order by t ③ evaluate ④ write back by row id row g t x (keep row ids) (inside group) per group 0 a 3 30 a: rows 0 2 4 ──► rows 2 4 0 ──► 10 30 60 ──► row g t x cs 1 b 1 100 b: rows 1 3 ──► rows 1 3 ──► 100 300 ──► 0 a 3 30 60 2 a 1 10 1 b 1 100 100 3 b 2 200 2 a 1 10 10 4 a 2 20 3 b 2 200 300 4 a 2 20 30 ``` - **`group_by().agg()` stops after ③**, one row per group (cheatsheet [diagram](../overview/polars-cheatsheet.qmd#sec-cs-summarise)). `.over()` adds ④: each result goes back to its row, so rows never move. - **Without `order_by=`, step ② is skipped.** "Previous" then means the previous row *in the frame*, whatever order the frame happens to be in. - **`mapping_strategy=` replaces ④** with a list per row or stacked results (@sec-win-mapping). ## Mechanics {#sec-win-mechanics} ::: {#ac49073a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import datetime as dt import polars as pl from pl_notes import datasets flights_df = datasets.flights().with_columns( # time_hour is the scheduled hour; add the minute for the exact scheduled departure sched_dep=pl.col("time_hour") + pl.duration(minutes=pl.col("minute")), ) weather_df = datasets.weather() penguins_df = datasets.penguins() toy_df = pl.DataFrame({ "g": ["a", "b", "a", "b", "a"], "t": [3, 1, 1, 2, 2], "x": [30, 100, 10, 200, 20], }) ``` ::: ### Partition keys {#sec-win-partition} One key, several keys (positional or a list), or any expression: ::: {#d135e4b3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} flights_df.select( "origin", "month", "dep_delay", origin_avg=pl.col("dep_delay").mean().over("origin"), origin_month_avg=pl.col("dep_delay").mean().over("origin", "month"), flights_that_day=pl.len().over(pl.col("sched_dep").dt.date()), ).head(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

To window a whole formula, wrap it: `(pl.col("x").cum_sum() - pl.col("x").sum()).over("g")` (z-score recipe in @sec-win-recipes). ### `order_by=`: order inside the window {#sec-win-order} ::: {#270f0c82 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} toy_df.with_columns( cs_rows=pl.col("x").cum_sum().over("g"), # frame order cs_t=pl.col("x").cum_sum().over("g", order_by="t"), # t order, as in the diagram first_t=pl.col("x").first().over("g", order_by="t"), # ≈ first(x, order_by = t) cs_all=pl.col("x").cum_sum().over(order_by="t"), # no partition: whole frame in t order ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: `order_by=` sorts inside each group, evaluates, and writes back, so the frame keeps its row order: dplyr's `lag(x, order_by = t)`, generalised to every expression. `toy_df.sort("t")` plus a plain `.over("g")` gives the same numbers in a new row order. That works when every window shares one order; `order_by=` lets windows differ and keeps the rows where they are. It takes several keys (`["t", "x"]`); `descending=` and `nulls_last=` are one bool for all keys, so for mixed directions order by an expression such as `-pl.col("t")`. Nulls in the key come first (@sec-win-nulls). ### `mapping_strategy=`: what comes back {#sec-win-mapping} ```text pl.col("x").sort(descending=True).head(2).over("g", mapping_strategy=...) group a → [30, 20] group b → [200, 100] "group_to_rows" (default) each group must return 1 value or exactly its own row count, else ShapeError "join" every row of the group gets the whole result as a list "explode" the results are stacked group after group: 4 rows, not 5 ``` Two values from the three-row group `a` can't map back to rows: ::: {#0d1619d9 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} toy_df.with_columns(top2=pl.col("x").sort(descending=True).head(2).over("g")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

This error occurred in the following expression:
	col("x").sort(desc).slice(offset=0, length=2).over([col("g")])
``` ::: ::: ::: `"join"` attaches the group's result to each of its rows. A scalar result stays a scalar, not a one-element list: ::: {#48c9c7ab .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} toy_df.with_columns( top2=pl.col("x").sort(descending=True).head(2).over("g", mapping_strategy="join"), avg=pl.col("x").mean().over("g", mapping_strategy="join"), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}

Planes with at least 500 flights (≈ `filter(n() >= 500, .by = tailnum)`): ::: {#4244fd22 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} flights_df.filter(pl.len().over("tailnum") >= 500)["tailnum"].unique().sort().to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ``` [None, 'N722MQ', 'N723MQ', 'N725MQ'] ``` ::: ::: The `None` is real: the 2,512 flights with no `tailnum` form one group, like `NA` in a dplyr group. Add `pl.col("tailnum").is_not_null()` to the filter. Top *n* and ties at the max are in @sec-win-recipes. ### Combining windows {#sec-win-nested} Each expression carries its own window, so one context can mix partitions, and a window can take another window's output. Rank the three airports by mean delay within each month (in dplyr, two chained `mutate(.by)` calls): the inner window computes the origin-month mean, the outer one ranks it within the month. ::: {#887315d6 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} flights_df.select( "month", "origin", origin_rank=pl.col("dep_delay").mean().over("origin", "month").rank("dense").over("month"), ).unique().sort("month", "origin_rank").head(6) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ```{=html}

What matters here is how nulls behave: ::: {#ae90018e .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} gaps_df = pl.DataFrame({"x": [1, None, 3, 4, None, 10]}) gaps_df.with_columns( lag=pl.col("x").shift(1), lead=pl.col("x").shift(-1), lag2=pl.col("x").shift(2, fill_value=0), diff=pl.col("x").diff(), pct=pl.col("x").pct_change(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}

There is no `cum_mean()`; `cum_sum() / cum_count()` skips nulls the same way. Dtypes: `cum_count()` is `UInt32`, and so is `cum_sum()` of a Boolean (a running count of `true`). `cum_sum()` widens `Int8`/`Int16` to `Int64`, but a `UInt32` column stays `UInt32`. ### Ranks and row numbers {#sec-win-rank} | `rank(method=)` | Ties get | R | dtype | |---|---|---|---| | `"average"` (default) | the mean of their positions | `rank(x)` | `Float64` | | `"min"` | the lowest position | `min_rank(x)` | `UInt32` | | `"max"` | the highest position | `rank(x, ties.method = "max")` | `UInt32` | | `"dense"` | consecutive integers, no gaps | `dense_rank(x)` | `UInt32` | | `"ordinal"` | distinct ranks, in row order | `row_number(x)` | `UInt32` | | `"random"` | distinct ranks, at random (`seed=`) | `rank(x, ties.method = "random")` | `UInt32` | : `rank()` methods {.striped} ::: {#26494fd4 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} ranks_df = pl.DataFrame({"x": [20, 10, 20, None, 30, 10]}) ranks_df.with_columns( average=pl.col("x").rank(), min=pl.col("x").rank("min"), max=pl.col("x").rank("max"), dense=pl.col("x").rank("dense"), ordinal=pl.col("x").rank("ordinal"), min_desc=pl.col("x").rank("min", descending=True), # ≈ min_rank(desc(x)) percent_rank=(pl.col("x").rank("min") - 1) / (pl.col("x").count() - 1), cume_dist=pl.col("x").rank("max") / pl.col("x").count(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ```{=html}

The default `None` means `window_size`, so a window that holds a null, or is still short at the start, gives null; `min_samples=1` skips nulls instead. The old name `min_periods` raises `ArgumentRemovedError` in 2.0. - **`center=True`**: with an even window the extra row goes before the current one (`rolling_mean(4, center=True)` covers *i* − 2 … *i* + 1). - **`weights=`** multiplies the window element-wise, oldest row first. `rolling_mean()` divides by the sum of the weights; `rolling_sum()` doesn't. On a column with nulls, weights raise a `PanicException` ("weights not yet supported on array with null values"): fill the nulls first. | R | Polars | |---|---| | `zoo::rollmeanr(x, 3, fill = NA)` | `rolling_mean(3)` | | `zoo::rollmean(x, 3, fill = NA)` (centred) | `rolling_mean(3, center=True)` | | `slider::slide_dbl(x, mean, .before = 2, .complete = TRUE)` | `rolling_mean(3)` | | `slider::slide_dbl(x, mean, .before = 2)` (partial windows) | `rolling_mean(3, min_samples=1)`, but nulls are skipped, not `NA` | | `slider::slide_dbl(x, mean, .before = 1, .after = 1, .complete = TRUE)` | `rolling_mean(3, center=True)` | | `mutate(m = slide_dbl(...), .by = g)` after `arrange(t)` | `rolling_mean(3).over("g", order_by="t")` | : Row-based rolling windows {.striped} ### Rolling windows by time {#sec-win-rolling-time} `rolling_*_by(by, window_size)` defines the window by a time (or integer) column instead of a row count. By default it is `(t − window_size, t]`: ::: {#e5167336 .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} times_df = pl.DataFrame({ "t": [dt.datetime(2013, 1, 1, h) for h in [0, 1, 1, 2, 5]], "x": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], }) times_df.with_columns( rows3=pl.col("x").rolling_sum(3, min_samples=1), right=pl.col("x").rolling_sum_by("t", "3h"), # (t − 3h, t] both=pl.col("x").rolling_sum_by("t", "3h", closed="both"), # [t − 3h, t] ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=15} ```{=html}

Beyond the built-ins, `pl.col("x").sum().rolling("t", period="3h")` runs *any* expression over a time window, and `df.rolling()` / `df.group_by_dynamic()` are the frame-level versions ([Time-Series Operations](../types/timeseries.qmd)). All three need a sorted index (@sec-win-sorted). Exponentially weighted windows are `ewm_mean()`, `ewm_std()` and `ewm_var()`. ## Where it bites {#sec-win-gotchas} | tidyverse behaviour | Polars behaviour | |---|---| | `arrange()` then `mutate(.by)` reads sorted rows | `.over()` reads frame order unless you pass `order_by=` | | `arrange()` puts `NA` last | `order_by=` puts nulls first, even with `descending=True` | | `cumsum()` turns everything after an `NA` into `NA` | `cum_*` skip nulls | | `percent_rank()` divides by the non-`NA` count | `pl.len()` counts nulls: divide by `.count()` | | ranks are integer or double | ranks are `UInt32` and wrap on subtraction | | `mutate()` always returns one row per input row | `mapping_strategy="explode"` changes the count and the order | : The differences at a glance {.striped} ### Row order is not time order {#sec-win-row-order} `flights` is stored by month, but in the order 1, 10, 11, 12, 2, …, and within a day by actual departure time with cancelled flights last: ::: {#4ab6c979 .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} flights_df["month"].unique(maintain_order=True).to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=17} ``` [1, 10, 11, 12, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9] ``` ::: ::: So `shift()`, `diff()` and `cum_*()` without `order_by=` compute "previous" in that order. Count the negative gaps between consecutive flights of a plane: ::: {#646108dd .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} flights_df.select( gaps_in_row_order=(pl.col("sched_dep").diff().over("tailnum") < pl.duration()).sum(), gaps_in_time_order=( pl.col("sched_dep").diff().over("tailnum", order_by="sched_dep") < pl.duration() ).sum(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=18} ```{=html}

It is the [expression `sort()` trap](../core/expressions.qmd#sec-expr-sort-trap) inside a window. `sort_by()` is safe only when the result leaves as a list or as new rows (`"join"`, `"explode"`, or inside `agg()`). ### `shift()` without `.over()` crosses groups {#sec-win-leak} Even on a sorted frame, a plain `shift()` hands the last value of one group to the first row of the next, like `lag()` without `.by`: ::: {#e8da2c36 .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} toy_df.sort("g", "t").with_columns( lag_frame=pl.col("x").shift(), lag_group=pl.col("x").shift().over("g"), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=20} ```{=html}

Sort by the index first (by group and index, if there are groups). ## Recipes {#sec-win-recipes} **Top *n* per group, with or without ties.** `rank("min")` keeps ties, like `slice_max(n = 3)`; `rank("ordinal")` returns exactly *n*. On both days, two flights share third place: ::: {#28efc2eb .cell execution_count=24} ``` {.python .cell-code} jan_df = flights_df.filter(pl.col("month") == 1, pl.col("day").is_in([20, 28])) jan_df.with_columns( delay_rank=pl.col("dep_delay").rank("min", descending=True).over("day"), ).filter(pl.col("delay_rank") <= 3).sort("day", "delay_rank", maintain_order=True).select( "day", "origin", "carrier", "dep_delay", "delay_rank" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=24} ```{=html}
